body.title: problem: Bypassing WebAuthn authentication during the password recovery process
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Unknown, I can't try it for some reason (please explain)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I use an on-premise instance as a private Git repository (<10 users)

### Problem description

For accounts where the only second authentication factor is a security key or a WebAuthn credential, with no TOTP authentication configured, the "Forgot Password" procedure allows anyone with access to the account's email address to set a new password and log in directly, without any WebAuthn authentication.

The 2FA enforcement policies and the admin interface correctly indicate that 2FA is active when only WebAuthn is enabled.
Consequently, we are led to believe that the account is secure, when in reality, the WebAuthn setup offers no more protection than a simple OTP sent via email.

Impossible to test on https://v18.next.forgejo.org : The "forgot password" form does nothing

### Potential workarounds

- Disable "forgot password"
- Enable TOTP, but unable to verify or enforce it for other users

### Forgejo Version

17.0.2

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

Docker

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*

body.title: bug: Credential failure 403 on pull-mirror sync and on new migration.
body.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

Yes, I've linked the repository below

### Description

Since upgrading to Forgejo v15 I can no longer synchronize my mirror of a git repo in AWS CodeCommit. There was no error message in the Forgejo UI, but no changes were synchronized after many minutes of waiting. I have pasted the portion of the log generated after clicking "Synchronize now" (with debug and git command logging enabled) and it clearly shows a credential problem.

I've tried a few things to narrow down the problem:

1. I confirmed that the credentials are correct by running a manual git dry run with interactive credentials from the command line on the same LXC running Forgejo. It synchronized correctly.

```bash
sudo -H -u git -- /usr/bin/git \
  -C /var/lib/forgejo/data/forgejo-repositories/<owner>/<mirror>.git \
  -c protocol.version=2 \
  -c credential.helper= \
  -c core.askPass= \
  fetch --dry-run --tags \
  'https://git-codecommit.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/v1/repos/<repo>/' \
  refs/heads/main
```

2. I tried creating a new migration of the same AWS git repo on both my Forgejo instance and on the official Forgejo test instance. Both failed with seemingly the same error:

```
Migrating from https://git-codecommit.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/v1/repos/<repo> failed.

migration failed: Clone: exit status 128 - fatal: unable to access 'https://git-codecommit.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/v1/repos/<repo>/': The requested URL returned error: 403
```

### Forgejo Version

15.0.10

### How are you running Forgejo?

I'm running Forgejo in an LXC running Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie) on Proxmox. I first created this container way back with Forgejo v7.0.5 by installing from binaries:

https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/installation/binary/

And I've upgraded from release to release successfully using these instructions:

https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/upgrade/

I've kept the Debian installation up to date as well.

I've not had any critical errors until now.

body.title: problem: add old-to-new URL redirects to Git-over-SSH
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I often change naming conventions and just need to rename stuff. Git repos and orgs are no difference. Forgejo is a perfect replacement for most of the things, with just one thing missing for me: **SSH repo redirects** on repo/org name changes.

### Problem description

GitHub allows me to rename a repo and sets up redirect to old repo. Now, Forgejo actually supports that too, but **only for HTTPS**, not for SSH. I would like it to also work for Git-over-SSH clones, which take up a majority of my deployment scenarios. The scenario is simple:
- User creates a new organisation and/or new repo.
- User clones this new repo using SSH URL (Git-over-SSH).
- User renames the organization or repo or both at the same time.
- Fetch/push now fails until I change the URL. This can be really hard to trace down as there can be many deployments of the same repo in our company. 

Now, Forgejo could just redirect as it does in Git-over-HTTPS, inform the user about the repo/org name change and potentially log the redirect so admin can trace this occurence and fix it without it breaking in the meantime. 

Of course, if the repo/org name has been shadowed by a new one, the redirect shouldn't happen at all, as GitHub or similar services do the same.

### Potential workarounds

I believe the fix is fairly simple, just add a few checks to `routers/private/serv.go` and a hook to `cmd/serv.go` which fires **only when the redirect happened** (`strings.EqualFold(results.OwnerName, username` and simillar `if` for the repo itself) and:
- Informs the client by sending a message like: `this repository has moved to %s/%s.\nplease update your remote: git remote set-url origin %s\n`
- Logs the redirect so an admin can trace it or SIEM can evaluate that it happened.

### Forgejo Version

v17.0.2, but tested also on `1a13355` (Next, commit from `2026-11-20`) and it still behaves the same.

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

I don't think this is relevant, but:
Forgejo v17.0.2
Git: several clients: 2.56.1 on Fedora 44, 2.47.3 on Debian 13

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*
